data.name: Eleutherius
data.gender_notes: Eleutherius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word eleutheria, meaning 'freedom, liberty'. In Christian tradition, St. Eleutherius was a bishop and martyr in Illyria. The name Eleutherius carries the meaning “Free, liberated” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Eleutherius usually hope their child will grow to embody free, liberated and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual freedom found through faith and devotion.
data.etymology: Eleutherius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, liberated.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eleutherius total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Eleutherius
in_english.meaning: Name means freedom, liberty, release, or deliverance
in_english.long_meaning: Originating from Greek root Ἕλευσμα (eleusma), meaning freedom, liberty, release. Eleutherius is a name associated with Saint Eleutherius, a 2nd-century bishop of Rome, known for his role in resolving the Quartodeciman controversy. This name symbolizes spiritual freedom, deliverance, and salvation. In Christian tradition, the name Eleutherius is associated with courage, resilience, and perseverance.

data.cultural_impact: St. Eleutherius is recognized as a patron saint of freedom and liberation. In the Middle Ages, he was invoked during regional uprisings to protect the inhabitants in their fight for independence. His feast day on the 22nd of October has been celebrated historically with feasts, prayers, and various rituals while groups struggled for their freedom.
data.spiritual_significance: Christians believe that St. Eleutherius embodies the essence of the Gospel message and shining a light onto the spiritual freedoms that are derived from a close relationship with God. Freedom from sin, fear, and despair, ultimately leading one to grow closer to the divine, and to live a more authentic, compassionate, and loving life. This corresponds to the spiritual freedom Christ alluded to in John 8:32, "If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free."
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eleutherius, derived from the Greek word 'eleutheros' meaning 'free,' symbolizes the liberation from sin and the promise of eternal freedom in Christ. It embodies the spiritual journey towards salvation, emphasizing the gift of God's grace that frees us from bondage to live an authentic and righteous life.

historical_references.reference: Saint Eleutherius was bishop of the ancient city of Illyricum, in the Roman province of Pannonia Inferior, in the 4th century.
historical_references.context: ancient city of Illyricum, Roman province of Pannonia Inferior

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Eleutherius continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Eleutherius in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Eleutherius, which means "Free, liberated". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
